candidates.title: Medium-normalized TEA vs TEOA
candidates.purpose: Test whether the TEA/TEOA CO/H2 difference in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system persists after tighter matching of medium-linked variables, versus shrinking when solvent and additive-derived composition are normalized.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4/MeCN:H2O/TEOA platform and identifies TEA as a plausible comparator within the same formulation family. EV061, EV013, GX009, and EV031 support the transferable concern that amines can change proton supply, CO2 association, viscosity, conductivity, and intermediate stability, so a donor substitution without composition control may confound identity with medium effects. The proposal transfers these observations into a stricter within-platform comparison; it does not assume the same mechanism is already established for Co-bpy.

comparisons.inference: Descriptive baseline comparator: whether an apparent TEA/TEOA selectivity difference is reproduced under the initially anchored recipe.
Primary discriminating contrast: if a difference remains after composition normalization, donor identity still matters beyond the matched medium variables controlled here.
Within-TEOA check for how much the normalization itself alters output; this is not a single-factor causal test of donor identity.
Within-TEA check for normalization sensitivity; large shifts indicate medium/composition confounding in the unnormalized donor comparison.

procedure: Verify one executable P01 baseline from the supplied literature record, then run a pilot to set component loadings, reactor fill, and sampling times that give quantifiable CO and H2 without detector saturation or complete deactivation.

Prepare the four groups with the same cobalt source, bpy, g-C3N4 batch, reactor geometry, light program, and CO2 handling; for normalized groups explicitly match MeCN/H2O and total amine-derived fraction across TEA and TEOA conditions.

Irradiate under identical timing and collect gas samples at common time points; include paired dark and no-CO2 checks in the same analytical campaign as external validity controls, but keep the main card focused on the four comparison groups.
Quantify CO and H2 for every group with the same calibration set and report amount and CO/H2 time profiles rather than a single endpoint selectivity only.

Compare whether TEA-versus-TEOA differences are similar in the anchored recipe and the normalized recipe, and record any concurrent changes in solution appearance or catalyst recovery only as covariates, not mechanistic proof.
measurements: CO/H2 ratio or selectivity versus time calculated from the jointly measured products.
Induction period or time-dependent drift in product formation, if present.
Pre- and post-run bulk pH or apparent acidity/basicity of the liquid phase as a covariate only.
Qualitative notes on precipitation, color change, or phase changes as comparability checks only; these cannot establish the active species.
candidates.supports: Supports H03 if a TEA/TEOA difference seen in the anchored recipe becomes substantially smaller or disappears in the composition-normalized comparison, while CO and H2 remain quantifiable in both normalized groups. That outcome would indicate that medium/proton-management or related composition effects contribute materially, without proving which one dominates.
candidates.refutes: Refutes the specific H03 emphasis if the TEA/TEOA difference is reproduced with similar direction and magnitude in both the anchored and normalized comparisons, suggesting that the controlled medium variables are not the main source of the selectivity difference. This would favor alternatives such as donor-specific redox or cobalt-state effects, though not uniquely prove them.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if catalytic output is too low or unstable for one or more groups, if normalized conditions cannot maintain comparable catalyst viability, if analytical uncertainty is of the same order as the observed TEA/TEOA difference, or if normalization changes multiple hidden properties so strongly that donor identity remains entangled with unmeasured variables.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature values. Select one literature-anchored TEOA baseline from P01 evidence, then pilot the smallest set of adjustable parameters needed for executable comparison: catalyst/loading window, illumination time, sampling interval, and gas calibration range. For normalized groups, match total liquid composition logic across TEA and TEOA by holding MeCN/H2O ratio and total amine-derived fraction constant; if physical handling or miscibility differs, document the deviation and treat resulting comparisons as partially confounded rather than forcing nominal equality.
candidates.limitations: Even the normalized comparison cannot isolate all donor-linked properties because TEA and TEOA differ in more than one chemical feature. Dissolved CO2, local proton activity, viscosity, and cobalt coordination are not directly measured here, so product changes alone cannot identify which medium effect is responsible. The P01 active cobalt species is not fully established, and support effects from g-C3N4 may mask or amplify donor differences.

candidates.title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures in TEA vs TEOA Co-bpy photocatalysis
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA give different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic features under matched P01 CO2-reduction conditions, consistent with different proton-management or hydrogen-containing states rather than a donor effect visible only in product ratios.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 supports using isotope substitution with operando spectroscopy to strengthen assignment of hydrogen-containing bands, but only as transferable method evidence. GX010 and GX015 support proton-inventory/isotope logic as a discriminator of proton-delivery environments, not as proof for this Co-bpy photocatalyst. EV031 supports the broader proposal that solvent/additive environment can change detectable intermediate populations and selectivity in bipyridine-based CO2 reduction. Proposed transfer: apply H2O/D2O substitution to matched TEA and TEOA P01 samples while keeping the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform fixed, and treat any isotope-sensitive signatures as evidence of differing hydrogen-coupled states, not direct identification of the catalytic mechanism.

comparisons.inference: Within TEOA, isotope-dependent band shifts or kinetic changes identify hydrogen-coupled observables worth tracking, but do not by themselves assign the catalytic intermediate.
Within TEA, isotope-sensitive features provide the matched comparator for whether TEA accesses similar or different hydrogen-coupled states.
Any donor-dependent difference in spectra under H2O is descriptive only until checked against isotope response; unchanged spectra would weaken a strong proton-management explanation.
Comparing TEA and TEOA under D2O tests whether donor-specific signatures persist when proton transfer is perturbed; persistence would leave cobalt-state or donor-redox explanations viable.

procedure: Prepare matched P01 baseline and TEA comparator samples using the same cobalt source, bipyridine source, g-C3N4 batch, solvent family, reactor geometry, CO2 handling, and acquisition timing; include a donor-free background if signal allows.

Run a short pilot to choose acquisition windows and concentrations/loadings that give reproducible catalyst-region and donor/solvent-region signals without saturation or severe baseline drift; if operando signal is too weak, switch to near-operando transfer with fixed delay and matched handling for all groups.
Acquire spectra under CO2 and illumination for H2O- and D2O-containing versions of TEA and TEOA samples, plus dark or donor-free backgrounds as needed for subtraction and assignment checks.
Track time-dependent appearance, shift, and decay of candidate bands or complementary signals, and align these observations with parallel product sampling only as correlation, not mechanistic proof.
measurements: Operando or near-operando IR band positions, intensities, and time profiles in regions plausibly sensitive to hydrogen-containing, CO2-derived, or ligand-associated species
Isotope-induced band shifts or attenuation upon H2O to D2O substitution
Difference spectra relative to dark and donor-free backgrounds
Replicate consistency of donor-dependent spectral features
Parallel CO and H2 product amounts from matched aliquots or matched runs to relate, not equate, spectral changes with catalytic output
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent isotope response: for example, TEOA and TEA show different H/D-sensitive bands, shift magnitudes, temporal behavior, or appearance/disappearance patterns under otherwise matched conditions, and these differences are larger than donor-free/background changes. Stronger support occurs if donor-specific spectral differences diminish or reorganize under D2O in a way that parallels weakening of TEA/TEOA CO/H2 divergence in matched catalytic runs.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, while spectra are dominated by shared features or non-isotope-sensitive changes only. If TEA/TEOA catalytic differences remain substantial in matched runs despite indistinguishable H/D-sensitive signatures, the proton-management-centered explanation is weakened relative to cobalt-state or donor-redox alternatives.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if signals are too weak, assignments remain ambiguous, isotope substitution materially changes multiple bulk properties at once, or TEA/TEOA differ in total signal quality because of baseline or scattering artifacts. A donor-dependent spectral difference without isotope sensitivity is also inconclusive for H03 because it may reflect cobalt speciation or donor photoredox effects instead.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent recipe numbers. Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation family and first verify exact baseline composition from supplied source records. Calibrate only the minimum needed variables: choose aqueous fraction, total optical density/path length, catalyst loading, and acquisition interval by pilot criteria of stable background, detectable catalyst-region signal, and reproducible CO/H2 readout in the matched baseline. For D2O substitution, keep nominal component identities and preparation order matched; if pH/pD matching is attempted, document the convention and use it consistently rather than claiming exact equivalence. If operando sensitivity is insufficient, predefine a switch to near-operando with identical transfer timing across groups.
candidates.limitations: This is a characterization proposal, not a proof of mechanism. Isotope-sensitive bands can show participation of hydrogen-coupled states but cannot uniquely establish their structure, rate-determining role, or product-forming relevance. TEA and TEOA alter several coupled variables at once, including donor identity and medium properties, so donor-to-donor contrasts remain partly confounded. D2O substitution changes more than proton mass, and recovered or delayed measurements may miss the true operating state.

candidates.title: CO2-associated donor speciation under matched P01 medium
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA create different detectable CO2-associated solution states in the P01 medium before illumination or after reaction-relevant equilibration, as a bounded indicator of donor-dependent local CO2/proton environment.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV029 and EV061 motivate checking whether TEOA can participate in CO2-associated adduct or ion-pair chemistry beyond electron donation. GX009 adds transferable concern that cobalt-bipyridine media can change with solvent coordination, water, viscosity, and conductivity. EV031 supports the broader idea that donor/solvent environment can alter observable intermediates and selectivity. Proposed transfer: in matched P01 solvent composition, compare TEA and TEOA by descriptive solution-state spectroscopy. This proposal does not assume the same adduct identity reported in other systems, and any observed bands or shifts would indicate association only, not the catalytic active state or causal mechanism by themselves.

comparisons.inference: Within TEA-containing medium, identifies CO2-induced spectral changes above the inert reference.
Within TEOA-containing medium, identifies CO2-induced spectral changes above the inert reference.
Tests whether TEA and TEOA differ in CO2-associated signatures under otherwise matched medium.

Tests whether any TEOA-specific CO2-associated signal exceeds the no-amine background; this is descriptive and does not isolate whether the signal comes from donor-CO2 association, donor-cobalt coordination, or both.

procedure: Prepare matched P01 media using the same cobalt source, bpy, g-C3N4 loading state, and solvent composition for all groups; equilibrate under inert gas or CO2 in the dark for a fixed pilot-validated time.
Acquire background spectra for solvent-only and component-minus-one references needed to subtract dominant solvent, support, and baseline cobalt-bpy features before assigning donor-dependent changes.
Measure each group by one primary solution-state method suitable for CO2-associated bands or shifts, with an orthogonal confirmatory method if pilot signal quality is sufficient.
If a CO2-dependent donor-specific feature appears, repeat on independently prepared samples and check reversibility by switching gas condition or brief degassing where chemically safe.
Record sample appearance, pH or apparent acidity metric where feasible, and conductivity or other simple covariates so spectral differences are not interpreted without medium-context notes.
measurements: Difference IR spectra of CO2-equilibrated minus inert-equilibrated samples, tracking new or shifted bands attributable to donor- or bicarbonate/carbonate-associated environments.
NMR chemical-shift or line-shape changes for donor-containing samples before and after CO2 equilibration, if the medium permits interpretable spectra.
Background-reference spectra for no-amine and component-minus-one samples to bound non-donor contributions.
Simple covariates such as apparent acidity metric and conductivity; these can contextualize medium changes but cannot establish molecular identity on their own.
Replicate consistency of any donor-specific CO2-responsive signal; reproducibility is required before using the signal in later catalytic correlation studies.
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference in CO2-responsive spectral features under matched P01 medium, especially if TEOA and TEA show distinct changes relative to their own inert references and the no-amine background. This would support a local CO2/proton-environment contribution, while remaining associational until linked to catalytic outcomes under the same controls.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03-dominant interpretation would be no reproducible donor-specific CO2-responsive difference despite adequate detection sensitivity and clean backgrounds, especially if TEA and TEOA appear spectroscopically similar under matched medium. That would weaken the case that donor-linked CO2-associated speciation is a main explanation, though it would not prove a redox-only mechanism.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if spectra are dominated by solvent/support overlap, if signals are near detection limits, if assignments depend on a single ambiguous band, or if donor substitution also changes uncontrolled covariates enough that the contrast becomes multi-factor in practice. Observing a new signal without assignment controls cannot establish adduct identity or catalytic relevance.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent fixed acquisition settings. Pilot first to choose sample concentration, path length, equilibration time, and whether IR, NMR, or both have usable signal-to-background in the actual P01 medium. Set the lowest concentration that still gives reproducible donor and CO2-responsive features without obvious precipitation or severe scattering from g-C3N4. Use the same preparation order, gas-contact protocol, and delay before measurement across groups. If g-C3N4 prevents interpretable solution-state spectra, run a matched clarified-supernatant variant as a bounded adaptation and label the transfer limitation explicitly rather than claiming fully equivalent operating chemistry.
candidates.limitations: This characterization is descriptive. A donor-specific CO2-responsive signal cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, the active cobalt state, or the cause of CO/H2 selectivity. g-C3N4 and cobalt-bpy may contribute overlapping features, and dark-equilibrated samples may miss illumination-generated states. If donor identity changes pH, coordination, or suspension properties simultaneously, the comparison remains mechanistically mixed even when composition is nominally matched.
